# File-lifecycle corpus

Files a person can bring to Lolly, and the files an intake path has to survive. The
corpus backs plan 203's rank 1 acceptance (every entry point, adversarial inputs,
measured peak memory) and its section 18 fixture set. `corpus.ts` builds every file;
`tests/file-intake-corpus.test.ts` runs each one through every door a file comes in
by and compares what happened with `outcomes.json`.

## Redistribution

Every file here can be redistributed. Most are generated byte by byte in `corpus.ts`
and are MPL-2.0, like the rest of this repository. They are written part by part and
compressed by the corpus's own DEFLATE writer, `deflate.ts`, so a mistake shared by a
Lolly writer and its reader cannot hide behind a round trip. Node's zlib is not used
to compress: builds that link different zlib versions compress the same input to
different bytes, and the sizes and declared lengths in `outcomes.json` would follow
them. The third-party files are the unchanged copies already committed elsewhere
under `tests/fixtures`, each under the licence recorded in its own folder. Nothing in
the corpus comes from a brand pack, and no SUSE material may be added.

The decompression bombs are built on demand from one repeated DEFLATE block that
inflates to 1 MiB of zeros, so a 400 MiB bomb costs about 420 KB and a few
milliseconds to make. Nothing large is committed.

## The doors

| Door | Entry function | What the run does |
|---|---|---|
| `gallery-drop` | `openDropChooser`, as the gallery's drop handler calls it | Takes "Unpack" or "Add to your library" when offered, otherwise cancels |
| `picker` | The asset picker's upload | A PDF or deck goes to its page importer; anything else to `storeUserUpload` |
| `utility-input` | `cappedFileRef` | Reads the file into Strip Hidden Data's file input, under its limit |
| `utility-convert` | `validateConvertFiles`, `convertSourceKind` | The Convert view's intake and kind detection |
| `pwa-launch` | `openLaunchedFiles` | The installed app's "Open with" launch queue |
| `pwa-share` | `initShareTargetFileIntake` | A file the service worker parked from the share sheet |
| `desktop-open` | `routeEvents` (`openFile`) | A file double-clicked on the desktop |
| `desktop-verb` | `routeEvents` (`openUtilityFile`) | The Dolphin "Strip data" verb, then the tool's seed read |
| `ios-open` | `initDeepLinkIntake` | A document opened in the iOS app, with the 48 MiB native limit |
| `android-share` | `initShareTargetIngest` | A file shared or opened on Android, with the 48 MiB native limit |
| `lolly-import` | `openLollyFile` | `.lolly` files only; takes the lead choice |

The doors that end at the "What should Lolly do?" sheet cancel it there, because past
the choice every one of them runs the gallery's code. The test drives them under jsdom
with an in-memory host. jsdom loads no media, so clips report no metadata at once, and
JPEG XL decoding needs a browser worker, so that fixture records the refusal Node gives.

## Running the corpus

```sh
node --import ./tests/css-stub.mjs --test tests/file-intake-corpus.test.ts
```

After a deliberate change in how a door treats a file, rewrite the known outcomes and
review the diff before committing it:

```sh
LOLLY_UPDATE_INTAKE_OUTCOMES=1 node --import ./tests/css-stub.mjs --test tests/file-intake-corpus.test.ts
```

Peak memory is the highest resident set size a worker thread samples every
millisecond during a run, less the resident set size when the run started. Each door
reports its highest peak in the test output. Adversarial fixtures run first and are
held to a budget. Memory the allocator keeps after a large run can hide part of a later
run's peak, so later figures are lower bounds. To keep every measurement:

```sh
LOLLY_INTAKE_MEMORY_REPORT=intake-memory.json node --import ./tests/css-stub.mjs --test tests/file-intake-corpus.test.ts
```

Write the measurements outside the repository, or under `plans/`: they describe one
machine.

## Device and installed-app checks

`write.ts` saves the corpus as real files, so the same inputs can be opened on a phone,
from a file manager or through an installed app:

```sh
node --import ./tests/css-stub.mjs tests/fixtures/file-lifecycle/write.ts <folder>
```

The folder must not exist yet. The 60 MiB clip is written as a sparse file. The bombs
are written as they are built, so keep that folder away from tools that unpack
archives on sight.

## Adding a fixture

Add it to `CORPUS` in `corpus.ts` with its families, what it holds and its source, add
its row here, then rewrite `outcomes.json` and read every line the diff adds. A file
from outside this repository needs a licence that allows redistribution, recorded
beside the file. A fixture that every path must refuse or contain is `adversarial`, and
the test holds it to a memory budget.
